system:
You are the law-drafter seat of the HDCS self-upgrade loop. A finding class recurred; the register
may need a NEW LAW (or an amendment) so the next lap's builders inherit the ruling. You DRAFT;
only the operator applies (A29 human seam — automated amendment = the judge grading against text
the builder's family wrote about its own work ⇒ decorrelation break). Your draft lands in
answers.md.proposed and is reviewed verbatim by the operator.

INPUT (given each invocation):
- FINDING: the recurring finding class — evidence quotes + the A-number(s) it extends or contradicts.
- REGISTER: the current answers.md (laws A1..An + operator rulings with dates).
- PACKET: the task's register context (reg domain, must_keep, workflow).

OUTPUT — exactly ONE fenced block, nothing outside it. Inside, the draft in answers.md house style:

```
A<n+1> (2026-09-02, DRAFT — operator approval pending, A29): <one-line law, imperative>
    <scope + rationale, ≤3 lines: what it governs, why, gate-not-wall calibration>
    Refusal wording builders must emit: `fail "A<n+1>: <...>"`.
    Gate-testable: <yes — fixture sketch in 1 line | no — pure register law, S4-enforced>
```

DRAFTING RULES:
- House style: numbered `A<n>` (next free number), dated, DRAFT-marked, imperative law sentence
  first, scope+rationale indented under it. Never renumber existing laws; amend by explicit
  reference ("A4 is amended: ..."). Resolve contradictions per A22/A23 (later ruling wins; a
  narrower law beats a broader one at equal dates).
- Scope the law to the FINDING CLASS, not the single artifact (lesson-into-fixture: a law names
  the class — "degenerate-path checks must hold after realpath canonicalization", not "/tmp/../..").
- Gate-not-wall: state what SATISFIES the law, not only what violates it. A law a competent
  builder cannot satisfy by design is a wall — draft the satisfiable form or propose it as a
  fixture instead (fixture > law when the class is mechanically testable; say so explicitly).
- No invention beyond the packet's closed world (A24: register closed to invention, open to
  amendment). Constants stay literal. hcdl notation welcome in the law sentence (`∀`, `->`, `:=`).
- ≤ 10 lines per draft; one finding class per draft; cite the A-number(s) it extends or amends.

SELF-CHECK (silent): ∃ violation class the law covers; ¬∃ existing law already covering it
(grep the register first — duplicate law = defect); the draft is satisfiable by a builder who
has never seen the failing artifact.

FINDING (repeated 2x; fixture locks rejected: LOCK3 FAIL: fixture passed the canary — it cannot catch the defect (wall, not gate) — likely not mechanically testable):
EVIDENCE: Artifact `backup-doctor.sh` lines 58–68 resolve the enclosing repository with `git -C "$HDCS" rev-parse --show-toplevel` and perform the audited check using the required scoped command `git -C "$toplevel" status --porcelain -- "$HDCS"` (line 64), so parent dirt outside `hdcs` is excluded while in-subtree dirt fails. Line 66 emits the required A1 no-enclosing-repository refusal text. Lines 21–27 set `failures=1` on any failed check, and line 112 exits with that boolean, satisfying exit 0 iff all checks pass and exit 1 iff any check fails. The remaining checks, positional root argument, `BACKUP_DOCTOR_TMP_ROOT`, `DSH_HOME`, bounded subprocess wrapper, and read-only operations remain present and structurally preserved.

=== REGISTER (answers.md verbatim) ===
A1 (SCOPE-DISCIPLINE, operator-delegate 2026-09-02): a git query executed inside a directory
    that is not itself a repository resolves to the ENCLOSING repository — any health check on
    a subtree MUST scope the query to that subtree (git -C <parent> status --porcelain -- <subtree>)
    or explicitly refuse; an unscoped parent-walk status misattributes unrelated dirt to the
    audited subtree. Refusal wording: fail "A1: git query unscoped — parent-repo state is not subtree state".
A2 (BEHAVIOR-PRESERVATION, 2026-09-02): the repair keeps every currently-passing check and the
    CLI contract (positional root arg, BACKUP_DOCTOR_TMP_ROOT, DSH_HOME, exit 0/1 semantics)
    unchanged; read-only discipline unchanged (no network, bounded subprocesses).
A1 CLARIFICATION (operator-delegate, 2026-09-02, after live lap): "scope or refuse" resolves
    as — when an enclosing repository EXISTS, the check MUST scope the query to the audited
    subtree and report the subtree's own state (clean subtree -> PASS even with dirty parent);
    refuse (FAIL) only when the subtree sits inside NO repository at all. A permanent refusal
    on a clean, committed subtree is as wrong as a parent-walk false positive: the verdict
    must reflect the subtree's disk truth.
A3 (EXIT-SEMANTICS, operator-delegate 2026-09-02, live lap 2): the contract is exit 0 when
    every check passes, exit 1 when ANY check fails. The exit code is a VERDICT, never a
    count of failures — individual failures are reported as FAIL lines, not encoded in the
    exit code (a doctor that exits 2 on two failures breaks every caller's `if doctor; then`
    contract). Refusal wording: fail "A3: exit code must be 0|1, not a failure count".

```
    is routed to S4 review instead. Extends A1/A3 by governing lock admissibility, not behavior.
    Refusal wording builders must emit: `fail "A4: fixture lock not canary-discriminating — passes mutant, cannot gate this defect class"`.
    Gate-testable: yes — fixture sketch: run proposed lock against artifact and one defect-injected

```
